next_step: Closed - lost to direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs; archive contact. Capture learnings and keep for future re-entry.
notes:
Summary: mid-market CS-focused startup building a conversational virtual agent (customer support) and on-site document search. POC started May '24. Primary driver = speed to market and low integration friction.

Key signals:
- Tech founder: 'We just need something that works fast; we can iterate later.'
- Procurement: heavy emphasis on vendor simplicity and brand recognition. OpenAI/Anthropic checked the UX boxes (SDKs, examples).
- Security: SOC2 + SSO required; security team OK with Redwood in principle but preferred vendor list and legal slow.

Why lost: Redwood perceived as higher initial integration/ops lift vs direct APIs. No internal champion after head of platform left in June. Budget freeze announced 2024-07-05 pending Q3 reforecast. Team decided to ship MVP with OpenAI (and test Anthropic) to reduce time-to-first-release.

Deal status: Closed - lost to OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs. Maintain warm relationship; left door open for Dedicated/Private if residency or audit controls become blocking for them later.

Quotes & color: 'We liked Redwood's observability and batching ideas, but we don't have the bandwith to run a custom runtime right now.' — Head of Platform.

Internal notes for AE/SE: capture eval logs (sweep KV/cache notes), keep pricing sensitivity notes (latency vs cost tradeoffs). Create a short one-pager on migration path from hosted API -> Dedicated/Private for future outreach.
timeline: 2024-05-02 - Lead created from website signup (trial credits)
2024-05-10 - Intro call (AE Maya Chen) - discussed use cases and SLO targets
2024-05-20 - Technical discovery w/ SE (Owen) - POC scope agreed (doc search + chat)
2024-07-05 - Internal budget freeze announced by customer
2024-07-09 - Procurement pushes preferred-vendor policy; legal recommends direct vendor APIs
2024-07-12 - Final decision: product team to proceed with OpenAI for MVP (informal)
decision_reason: Chose OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs for simpler integration, faster time-to-MVP, and brand trust; Redwood judged more feature-rich but higher initial ops effort. No internal champion remained to drive a longer evaluation.
